newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's TCV to repay A$4.537 bln debt 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Australia's TCV to repay A$4.537 bln debt 96/97.

text.p: Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) said on Tuesday it will repay A$4.537 billion in state debt in 1996/97 (July-June) following Tuesday's sale of the Victorian state assets in Loy Yang Power Ltd.

Earlier, the Victorian government announced the sale of its Loy Yang A generating station for A$4.855 billion, producing proceeds for the state of A$4.75 billion, which would be applied to reduce the state's net debt.
Surplus investments arising from the state's sale of the Hazelwood Power Corporation in August 1996 were fully applied to debt retirement by February 1997.
The proceeds of the Loy Yang A sale would be progressively applied to the reduction of TCV's gross debt as maturities and market opportunities arose, said TCV, the Victorian state's borrowing arm.

"Significant progress has been made during the current year on the early retirement of international securities and further opportunites are anticipated. TCV will maintain its commitment to appropriate levels of hot stock outstandings," said David Carruthers, TCV's Managing Director.
